alt: Two people arrange household money, a calendar and everyday objects around a shared written plan.
A person sorts money already on the table into trays for household purposes; future income remains separate.
Future income is committed to a debt folder; after that folder closes, the calendar becomes clear space again.
An envelope set aside from existing household money is offered to another person with dignity.
A small everyday payment tray connects through a conversion step to a separate long-term money reserve.
Money, household consumption assets and productive tools are laid out as distinct parts of one balance sheet.
A traveler compares a map with uneven terrain, illustrating the difference between a model and the path actually travelled.
A person weighs useful consumption, retained money and a productive tool as three different uses of capital.
Two household members review accessible instructions together so the financial plan does not depend on one person.
A household writes its money policy and schedules repeated reviews rather than treating the plan as finished.
